quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard tells you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign shows you are near a school. Stay alert and stop if children are crossing.

questions.question: What should you know about shifting gears while turning?

options.text: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
It is better than shifting before you turn.
It is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can make your motorcycle skid.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is next to the right handgrip. Know where all your controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, what may you need to do?

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before you downshift safely.
Speed up before you downshift safely.
Flash your brakes so drivers behind you know you are downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before you downshift safely.
questions.explanation: Before shifting to a lower gear, slow down enough to shift safely. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: How often should you do head checks?

options.text: Rarely, because they take your eyes off the road.
Often as part of your normal routine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often as part of your normal routine.
questions.explanation: Check your surroundings often. Only by knowing what is happening around you can you prepare for hazards.

questions.question: When your motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, what can you do?

options.text: Use less pressure on the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel gets more grip on the road. This means you can brake harder with the front brake.

questions.question: How should a rider prevent injury on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down on slippery surfaces. Sudden moves can cause skids. Do not use the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane
No part of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best or always bad. Choose a position based on riding conditions.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
When you start to lose control in a curve.
When the motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If your throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch at the same time. This cuts power to the rear wheel so you can stop safely.

questions.question: What does this red and white sign tell you to do?

options.text: Stop and look both ways before you go.
Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
Keep the same speed and check all directions for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
questions.explanation: A yield sign with three sides means you must slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let any cars, bikes, or pedestrians pass first. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is merging in from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging in from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that traffic will be entering from the right.

questions.question: Why should you keep a safe distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: So you have time to see and react to dangers.
So you can follow closely behind them.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you have time to see and react to dangers.
questions.explanation: A safe distance gives you room to stop or move if the car ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of the road ahead so you can spot problems like potholes.

questions.question: When should you use more space between you and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: A two-second distance is normal. Use more space when conditions make it harder to stop, such as wet or icy roads.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look better.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol they drink.
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by three main things: how much alcohol someone drinks, how fast they drink it, and their body weight.

questions.question: When someone passes you from behind, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Stay on the left side of your lane.
Stay in the middle of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: The middle of your lane is safest when being passed. Riding near the passing car increases crash risk. Riding far from it might make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Get them a safe ride home.
Give them other activities to do instead of drinking.
Keep them from leaving until they are sober.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Never let an impaired friend ride a motorcycle. Instead, arrange safe transportation, distract them with other activities, keep them from leaving before they are sober, and ask other friends to help you stop them.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic going the same direction?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent problems. Small issues on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Without signaling, so you don't distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal your intention, check for traffic, and pass only when safe. Signal again and return to your original lane when possible.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass you.
questions.explanation: Let tailgaters pass you. If you speed up, they will likely continue tailgating at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What is often found in the center portion of a traffic lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Oil drippings from cars form a strip in the center of each lane. Unless it's wet, a motorcycle can usually ride safely on this center strip.

questions.question: Why should you ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass?

options.text: It increases your line of sight.
It decreases your line of sight.
It makes it difficult to see beyond the vehicle.
It allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases your line of sight.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to see more ahead and to be more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right part of the lane so they can see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of the lane to increase your line of sight.
Stay in the center part of the lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of the lane to increase your line of sight.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to see ahead better and to be more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: When do you not need a larger space cushion?

options.text: When you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: When weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: You need extra space when conditions are bad. Increase your following distance if pavement is slippery, visibility is poor, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping, how should you shift gears?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How often will you hear a tire going flat?
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists seldom hear a tire going flat. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is the usual sign of a tire problem.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam headlight when there are no other vehicles nearby, and stay far behind other vehicles. Watch the headlights and taillights of vehicles ahead. Their lights help you see the road and warn you about bumps.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. If you notice a change in handling, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that you cannot turn in the direction the arrow points. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, you should:

options.text: Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as a train passes.
Wait to proceed until you can see all tracks clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait to proceed until you can see all tracks clearly.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see down all the tracks clearly before you cross. Another train may be coming.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while you are riding, the steering will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, exit the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Using your brakes too hard can cause you to lose grip on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards since there are very few on the road.
Look ahead but avoid looking for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Always look far ahead while riding to spot dangers early. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Be alert for construction workers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that pedestrians may cross the road ahead. Drive carefully in these areas.

questions.question: How do convex mirrors differ from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a better view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are used on many motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.
